title: Determination of the Property Credit Drawn Down on a Hotel Rate Plans Stay
content:
This determination settles how much property credit a guest draws down against what they have taken at the property on a Hotel Rate Plans reservation.

## 1. The credit standing

The credit standing is the largest single grant posted on the reservation together with whatever has already been drawn against it, which is carried as a negative figure.

## 2. What is available and what it may be spent against

0 percent of the credit standing is available.

0 percent of the minibar charges posted is counted as a charge the credit may be spent against.

The eligible spend is nothing.

## 3. The credit drawn down

The credit drawn down is the smaller of the credit available and the eligible spend, and is never less than nothing.

Every figure is rounded to two decimal places as it is worked out, and the credit drawn down is rounded the same way.

## 4. Worked on hypothetical figures

Take a reservation whose folio carries two property credit grants, of 100.00 USD and 50.00 USD, against which 40.00 USD has already been drawn, and minibar charges of 85.00 USD.

1. The largest single grant posted is 100.00 USD, and the 40.00 USD already drawn is carried as a negative figure, so the credit standing is 60.00 USD.
2. The credit available is 0 percent of 60.00 USD, which is 0.00 USD.
3. Of the 85.00 USD of minibar charges posted, 0 percent is counted as a charge the credit may be spent against, which is 0.00 USD.
4. The eligible spend is nothing, which is 0.00 USD.
5. The credit drawn down is the smaller of 0.00 USD and 0.00 USD, and is not below nothing. It is **0.00 USD**.

Had nothing yet been drawn against the grants, the credit standing would be 100.00 USD, and the credit drawn down would still be 0.00 USD.
